title: Cops felt injury faked, jurors told
article: When Bryan Dukic's legs gave out and his body became limp as two Windsor police officers walked him to the police transport wagon in handcuffs -- less than three hours before he died from massive internal hemorrhaging caused by a ruptured spleen -- Const. Richard Sieberer thought Dukic was "faking," a coroner's inquest heard Wednesday.

"He's still talking to us and all of a sudden he can't move his body," said Sieberer, who was in an altercation with Dukic on April 5, 2006, along with his partner Const. John Ryan, as they tried to place the 42-year-old under arrest behind a Russell Street apartment building.
Sieberer said he thought Dukic was faking illness in an attempt to avoid being placed in the wagon -- a tactic he's seen many detainees use to delay going to jail, he said.
It wasn't until Dukic fell from a kneeling position and struck his head on the pavement that Sieberer said he realized something was really wrong.

Both Sieberer and Ryan described a combative Dukic, who they said resisted being handcuffed, yelled profanities and threatened one of the officers. Around 6:20 p.m. that evening, the two officers followed a Dodge Caravan Dukic was driving to a rear lot behind the building and told him he was under arrest because he was a disqualified driver. Dukic did not have a driver's licence on him. His passenger, Brian Lacroix, who was known to police, produced an expired licence.
The officers said they followed the Dodge Caravan because it was suspected of frequenting a suspected drug house in the area, where Lacroix lived.

Both officers testified that Dukic told them he'd just got out of jail and did not want to go back. When they tried to handcuff him, he started flailing his arms and ran into a nearby field. Dukic was "swinging, twisting" and kicking out his legs, striking the officers and ripping one of their jackets, the inquest heard. Ryan punched Dukic four or five times in the head while Sieberer kneed Dukic in the ribs before handcuffing him.

Sieberer told jurors the altercation lasted about two minutes. While Ryan testified that the punches he delivered to Dukic's head were meant to "distract" him so that he would give up his arms for handcuffing, Sieberer admitted he kneed Dukic as hard as he could, under cross-examination by Dukic family lawyer Gino Morga.
Asked whether Ryan also punched Dukic "as hard as he could," Sieberer said: "I would hope so.... I would hope for my safety that my partner would punch him as hard as he could."
When the police transport wagon arrived just after 7 p.m., Dukic complained that his ribs were sore and he had trouble breathing.
Const. Marcus Marentette, who drove the wagon that night, testified that Dukic looked "jaundiced" when he arrived.
"Right away I had reservations about transporting him," Marentette said.
He testified that he asked Dukic if he was ill or on medication. Dukic shook his head and mumbled "No," but Marentette told the officers the detainee should still get a medical assessment.

Sieberer said he told that Dukic had a previous fight with someone, suffered from hepatitis C and was involved in "a short struggle in the field" with police. Under questioning from Morga, he denied hiding the fact that Dukic was punched and kicked.

One of the paramedics, Robin Smallwood, testified Tuesday he wasn't told that Dukic was struck several times or kicked in the ribs. Ryan testified Wednesday that Dukic's breathing was "fine" and he was talking to the officers until the paramedics arrived.
